issues.description: The specification/UML requires Rideable.messageOnRide() with no parameters returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements it accordingly in Pig and Seal. This contradicts the stated interface contract and expected output format, and would confuse students about the required method signature and behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution (and intended design) with the problem statement by changing Rideable to `String messageOnRide()` (no parameters) and updating Pig/Seal to return exactly `"Riding on Pig/Seal " + getName()`; alternatively, if speed is intended, update the UML/problem statement text and examples to include the `int speed` parameter and the corresponding output format.

issues.description: The template Farm.singFarmSongVerse method is stubbed without an Animal parameter (commented out), while both the UML and the solution require `singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal)`. As written, the template signature prevents students from implementing the required per-animal verse logic without changing the method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template signature to `private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)` and add/import the Animal type (once created), matching the UML/solution.

issues.description: The Rideable interface method is specified as messageOnRide():String in the problem statement/UML, but the solution implements messageOnRide(int speed) with a speed parameter. This changes the identifier signature for the same conceptual operation (riding message), making it unclear to students which method to implement to satisfy the requirements.
issues.suggestedFix: Align Rideable to the UML/statement by changing Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) to Rideable.messageOnRide() and update Pig/Seal accordingly (remove the speed parameter and adjust returned strings), or alternatively update the problem statement/UML and template to consistently require messageOnRide(int speed) everywhere.

issues.description: The template Farm.singFarmSongVerse is declared without an Animal parameter (commented as /*Animal animal*/), while the problem statement/UML and solution both define singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal). This mismatch makes the helper method’s intended signature unclear when mapping requirements to the starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template to declare singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) exactly as in the UML/statement (and as used by singFarmSong), removing the commented placeholder to avoid signature ambiguity.
